summary: The proposal addresses a relevant problem and sketches a plausible Artemis–GitLab CI integration, but it is not ready for submission. Critical structural omissions, insufficient figures and references, the missing AI transparency statement, and an underdeveloped objective section must be addressed first; the schedule, stakeholder analysis, and writing also require substantial revision.

findings.title: Missing Introduction section
findings.description: The required Introduction section is missing. Add it before the Problem section and briefly establish the context, scope, and purpose of the proposed work.

findings.title: Missing Motivation section
findings.description: The required standalone Motivation section is missing. Explain the scientific and educational importance of solving the problem, why the proposed approach is needed, and the positive vision of a reliable, adaptable, and lower-maintenance assessment infrastructure. The combined “Motivation/Objective” label in the abstract does not replace this section.

locations.quote: Since some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to reduce the efort required to maintain the servers and migrate the CI service from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt CI service.
The interactive learning platform Artemis currently only supports setups with an external CI server.

Artemis currently supports Bamboo and Jenkins as a CI server for executing the tests. This leads to additional server overhead, since the CI and the Version Control (VC) are running on diferent servers.

findings.title: Missing Objective section and required subsections
findings.description: The required Objective section (Section 4) is missing. Replace the current “System Requirements and Top Level Design” Section 4 with an objective section containing a short introduction, a one-line bullet list of 3–4 high-level objectives, and one subsection for each objective. Each subsection must contain at least two paragraphs describing the objective’s scope, intended outcome, and evaluation. Use direct, action-oriented formulations rather than passive or compound statements.

findings.title: Missing AI transparency statement
findings.description: The proposal does not contain an AI transparency statement. Add a dedicated first-person statement naming each AI tool used, explaining its purpose, identifying the sections in which it was used, and confirming that all AI-generated text was checked for correctness and coherence.

findings.title: Problem section proposes functionality

locations.quote: The CI server should be migrated to the VC server.
This system supports the provision of the build plan via the Artemis API, which makes it possible to update the build plan retrospectively, as the build plan is fetched from the API on each run.

Since some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to reduce the efort required to maintain the servers and migrate the CI service from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt CI service.
Furthermore, it should be possible to adjust the build plan after the task has been assigned.
This system supports the provision of the build plan via the Artemis API, which makes it possible to update the build plan retrospectively, as the build plan is fetched from the API on each run.

To achieve this goal, Artemis uses a Version Control (VC) and Continuous Integration (CI) server, to execute test cases predefned by the instructor on each submission of each student, display the build results and grade the submission [Krusche18].
Later changes to the base build plan are not patched automatically to all student build plans, but rather the build plans must be updated manually in the CI Server.
Additionally, the base build plan is copied once after the student started the exercise [Krusche18].
Furthermore, the CI service should be part of the VC server to reduce additional efort by maintaining two servers.
As a result, instructors are able to update the build plan after the release of an exercise, GitLab CI fetches the updated build plan when needed.
In order to implement this idea, the lecture is split up into multiple iterations, each consisting of diferent phases [Krusche17].

Since the benefts of using CI are quite high and nearly half of the developers who do not use CI mention a lack of familiarity as the reason for not using a CI service, it is useful to teach the concepts of CI at university [Hilton16].
Not only projects using CI release twice as often as projects without CI, but the build is also less likely to fail in the master branch [Hilton16].
